Listing fields vs App Intents engineering vs screenshot design

Intent-aware apps blur three workstreams indie teams conflate:

  • App Store Connect listing metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshot overlay captions on the zh-Hans row. AppLocale scope.
  • App Intents / SiriKit / Shortcuts runtime — intent definitions, AppShortcutsProvider, parameter summaries, localized intent titles inside iOS, Apple Intelligence model hooks. Engineering scope — not AppLocale.
  • Screenshot composition — device frames, Siri sheet mockups, Shortcuts tile layouts, re-exporting PNGs with burned-in action phrases. Design scope — AppLocale delivers caption lines you paste or hand to a designer.

This page covers the first bucket for intent-centric product pages. It is not our generic screenshot captions guide (any app gallery), not our widget gallery guide (Home Screen / Lock Screen widgets), and not our Live Activities guide (Dynamic Island live updates).

Why intent-gallery English hurts on the China storefront

Apps that market Siri and Shortcuts often lead screenshots with system-style surfaces where English chrome and your action phrases appear together:

  • English frame headlines — “Siri”, “Shortcuts”, “Ask Siri to…” left as capture defaults while your zh-Hans description claims full Chinese support
  • Action-phrase overlays — “Start my workout”, “Log today’s mood”, “Create a reminder” still in Latin script on gallery frames buyers skim before reading the description
  • Shortcuts tile labels — intent titles and parameter chips visible in marketing captures that do not match 快捷指令 search intent
  • Apple Intelligence action chips — on-device action surfaces with English micro-copy when productivity or utility buyers browse in zh-Hans locale
  • Searchable fields still English — subtitle and keywords never packed for 快捷指令, 语音控制, or Siri-adjacent terms Chinese users actually type

Better zh-Hans listing copy and intent-screenshot captions reduce product-page bounce for Siri-aware buyers — they do not replace App Intents localization inside the binary, change Shortcuts behavior at runtime, or guarantee Search rank.

Common mistakes on App Intents app zh-Hans listings

  • Translating only the description — name, subtitle, and keywords still English while Siri/Shortcuts screenshots dominate the gallery
  • Pasting 快捷指令 into every keyword slot — crowding the 100-character field without room for your app’s actual use case (habit, finance, fitness)
  • English action phrases in PNG exports — Connect caption fields are zh-Hans but burned-in “Ask Siri to…” overlays on the image file are still Latin
  • Assuming intent title localization = listing done — runtime Shortcuts tile names can be Chinese while the App Store row still falls back to English
  • What's New still English after intent launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when App Intents shipped in a recent version
  • Generic utility copy — description written for the main app with one sentence mentioning Siri instead of naming voice actions and Shortcuts workflows
  • Literal 翻译腔 on Siri jargon — awkward translations of “App Intent” or “Shortcuts automation” that native readers do not use in App Store copy
  • Confusing ChatGPT listing work with intent listing work — an AI chat app page is not the same as an App Intents / Siri / Shortcuts product story

What good zh-Hans intent listing copy looks like

Listing fields should name the voice and automation surfaces you actually ship — aligned with your screenshot order:

  • Subtitle — one concrete promise: “支持 Siri 与快捷指令” or “语音启动，一步完成” — not vague “提升效率”
  • Keywords — mix category terms (待办, 健身, 记账) with automation terms (快捷指令, 语音) within Connect’s ~100-character zh-Hans budget; see Simplified Chinese keywords guide
  • Description — short paragraphs for Siri voice commands, Shortcuts tiles, and Apple Intelligence actions if you market them — mirror screenshot sequence
  • Screenshot captions on intent frames — name the on-screen action: “对 Siri 说「开始专注」” not “强大功能”
  • Action-phrase caption lines — when your gallery shows example Siri invocations, caption sheet lists zh-Hans equivalents for designer re-export
  • Optional spoken phrase suggestions — when you include English action phrases in your brief, we can suggest natural zh-Hans spoken equivalents for marketing reference — not App Intents code changes
  • Voice consistency — same 你/您 choice as your description across overlay lines and promotional text

Connect checklist for App Intents apps targeting China

  1. Open App Store → Chinese (Simplified) — confirm the zh-Hans row exists; empty rows fall back to English on the China storefront
  2. Audit searchable fields — name, subtitle, keywords, description saved in zh-Hans, not placeholder English
  3. Walk the screenshot gallery in order — flag frames showing Siri sheets, Shortcuts tiles, Ask Siri prompts, or action-phrase overlays
  4. Export overlay lines — spreadsheet of English caption text per frame beats screenshots of Connect alone
  5. Note burned-in vs Connect captions — if action phrases are embedded in PNGs, caption deliverables go to your designer for re-export
  6. List English spoken phrases optionally — if you want suggested zh-Hans equivalents in the deliverable, include them in your intake brief
  7. Match What's New if intents are new — release notes should mention Siri/Shortcuts support in zh-Hans when that version added App Intents
  8. Verify China in Pricing and Availability — storefront enabled before expecting zh-Hans to appear
